Predicting with Quantile Regression Forests#

This example demonstrates the use of a quantile regression forest (QRF) to predict the conditional median and construct prediction intervals. The noisy samples are generated from the function f(x) = x sin(x) plus right-skewed noise that grows with x, so the conditional median lies below f(x) and the intervals are asymmetric. The QRF predictions are compared to the true conditional median and 95% interval, which are known for this toy dataset.

import altair as alt
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import scipy as sp
from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split
from sklearn.utils.validation import check_random_state

from quantile_forest import RandomForestQuantileRegressor

random_state = np.random.RandomState(0)
n_samples = 1000
bounds = [0, 10]
quantiles = [0.025, 0.5, 0.975]


def make_toy_dataset(n_samples, bounds, add_noise=True, random_state=None):
    """Make a toy dataset."""
    random_state = check_random_state(random_state)

    x = random_state.uniform(*bounds, size=n_samples)
    f = x * np.sin(x)

    sigma = 0.25 + x / 20
    noise = random_state.lognormal(sigma=sigma) - np.exp(sigma**2 / 2)
    y = f + (noise if add_noise else np.zeros_like(f))

    return np.atleast_2d(x).T, y


def get_true_quantiles(x, quantiles):
    """Get the true quantiles of the toy dataset's noisy targets at `x`."""
    sigma = 0.25 + x / 20
    z = sp.stats.norm.ppf(quantiles)  # quantiles of the lognormal noise's exponent
    return (
        x[:, None] * np.sin(x[:, None])
        + np.exp(sigma[:, None] * z)
        - np.exp(sigma**2 / 2)[:, None]
    )


# Create a noisy dataset for modeling and evenly spaced inputs for illustration.
X, y = make_toy_dataset(n_samples, bounds, add_noise=True, random_state=0)
X_func = np.linspace(*bounds, num=n_samples).reshape(-1, 1)
y_func = get_true_quantiles(X_func.ravel(), quantiles)

X_train, X_test, y_train, y_test = train_test_split(X, y, random_state=random_state)

qrf = RandomForestQuantileRegressor(min_samples_leaf=10, random_state=random_state)
qrf.fit(X_train, y_train)

y_pred_test = qrf.predict(X_test, quantiles=quantiles)  # predict on noisy samples
y_pred_func = qrf.predict(X_func, quantiles=quantiles)  # predict on evenly spaced inputs

df = pd.DataFrame(
    {
        "x": np.concatenate([X_test.reshape(-1), X_func.reshape(-1)]),
        "y": np.concatenate([y_test, y_func[:, 1]]),
        "y_low": np.concatenate([np.full(len(y_test), np.nan), y_func[:, 0]]),
        "y_upp": np.concatenate([np.full(len(y_test), np.nan), y_func[:, 2]]),
        "y_pred": np.concatenate([y_pred_test[:, 1], y_pred_func[:, 1]]),
        "y_pred_low": np.concatenate([y_pred_test[:, 0], y_pred_func[:, 0]]),
        "y_pred_upp": np.concatenate([y_pred_test[:, 2], y_pred_func[:, 2]]),
        "test": [True] * len(y_test) + [False] * len(y_func),
    }
)


def plot_predictions_and_intervals(df):
    """Plot model predictions and prediction intervals with ground truth."""
    area_pred = (
        alt.Chart(df)
        .transform_filter(~alt.datum["test"])  # filter to non-test data
        .mark_area(color="#e0f2ff", opacity=0.8)
        .encode(
            x=alt.X("x:Q", scale=alt.Scale(nice=False), title="X"),
            y=alt.Y("y_pred_low:Q", title=""),
            y2=alt.Y2("y_pred_upp:Q", title=None),
            tooltip=[
                alt.Tooltip("x:Q", format=",.3f", title="X"),
                alt.Tooltip("y:Q", format=",.3f", title="True Median"),
                alt.Tooltip("y_pred:Q", format=",.3f", title="Predicted Median"),
                alt.Tooltip("y_pred_low:Q", format=",.3f", title="Predicted Lower Y"),
                alt.Tooltip("y_pred_upp:Q", format=",.3f", title="Predicted Upper Y"),
            ],
        )
    )

    circle_test = (
        alt.Chart(df.assign(**{"point_label": "Test Observations"}))
        .transform_filter(alt.datum["test"])  # filter to test data
        .mark_circle(color="#f2a619")
        .encode(
            x=alt.X("x:Q", scale=alt.Scale(nice=False)),
            y=alt.Y("y:Q", title=""),
            color=alt.Color("point_label:N", scale=alt.Scale(range=["#f2a619"]), title=None),
            tooltip=[
                alt.Tooltip("x:Q", format=",.3f", title="X"),
                alt.Tooltip("y:Q", format=",.3f", title="Y"),
            ],
        )
    )

    line_true = (
        alt.Chart(df.assign(**{"y_true_label": "True Median"}))
        .transform_filter(~alt.datum["test"])  # filter to non-test data
        .mark_line(color="gray", size=2)
        .encode(
            x=alt.X("x:Q", scale=alt.Scale(nice=False)),
            y=alt.Y("y:Q", title="Y"),
            color=alt.Color(
                "y_true_label:N",
                scale=alt.Scale(range=["gray"]),
                legend=alt.Legend(symbolType="stroke", symbolStrokeWidth=2),
                title=None,
            ),
            tooltip=[
                alt.Tooltip("x:Q", format=",.3f", title="X"),
                alt.Tooltip("y:Q", format=",.3f", title="True Median"),
            ],
        )
    )

    line_true_interval = (
        alt.Chart(df.assign(**{"y_true_interval_label": "True 95% Interval"}))
        .transform_filter(~alt.datum["test"])  # filter to non-test data
        .transform_fold(["y_low", "y_upp"], as_=["bound", "y_bound"])
        .mark_line(color="gray", size=2, strokeDash=[4, 4])
        .encode(
            x=alt.X("x:Q", scale=alt.Scale(nice=False)),
            y=alt.Y("y_bound:Q", title=""),
            detail="bound:N",
            color=alt.Color(
                "y_true_interval_label:N",
                scale=alt.Scale(range=["gray"]),
                legend=alt.Legend(symbolType="stroke", symbolStrokeWidth=2, symbolDash=[4, 4]),
                title=None,
            ),
            tooltip=[
                alt.Tooltip("x:Q", format=",.3f", title="X"),
                alt.Tooltip("y_low:Q", format=",.3f", title="True Lower Y"),
                alt.Tooltip("y_upp:Q", format=",.3f", title="True Upper Y"),
            ],
        )
    )

    line_pred = (
        alt.Chart(df.assign(**{"y_pred_label": "Predicted Median"}))
        .transform_filter(~alt.datum["test"])  # filter to non-test data
        .mark_line(color="#006aff", size=4)
        .encode(
            x=alt.X("x:Q", scale=alt.Scale(nice=False)),
            y=alt.Y("y_pred:Q", title=""),
            color=alt.Color("y_pred_label:N", scale=alt.Scale(range=["#006aff"]), title=None),
            tooltip=[
                alt.Tooltip("x:Q", format=",.3f", title="X"),
                alt.Tooltip("y:Q", format=",.3f", title="True Median"),
                alt.Tooltip("y_pred:Q", format=",.3f", title="Predicted Median"),
            ],
        )
    )

    # For desired legend ordering.
    blank = (
        alt.Chart(pd.DataFrame({"y_area_label": ["Predicted 95% Interval"]}))
        .mark_area(color="#e0f2ff")
        .encode(
            color=alt.Color("y_area_label:N", scale=alt.Scale(range=["#e0f2ff"]), title=None),
        )
    )

    # Draw the true median over the predicted median too, where they overlap.
    line_true_top = line_true.encode(color=alt.value("gray"))

    chart = (
        (
            area_pred
            + circle_test
            + line_true
            + line_true_interval
            + line_pred
            + line_true_top
            + blank
        )
        .resolve_scale(color="independent")
        .properties(title="QRF Predictions vs. Ground Truth on Toy Dataset", height=400, width=650)
    )

    return chart


chart = plot_predictions_and_intervals(df)
chart
